title: Reef corals breathe by spinning tiny vortices — heat can break the pump
summary: Scientists filmed the cilia-driven pump in the boulder coral Porites lutea and found it speeds up then fails above about 37C in acute lab warming in darkness, shifting oxygen supply from stirring to slow diffusion — a threshold that varies by species and conditions.

claims.text: Corals actively regulate oxygen and metabolite exchange across the coral-water interface via cilia-induced vortical flows that stir the concentration boundary layer (CBL), rather than relying solely on passive diffusion.
